objective.statement: Write a new rest for each silent beat.
successCriteria: I know each silent beat normally gets its own rest.
I know a rest should not join two beats in a bar of triple time.
I know a whole bar of silence has its own whole-bar rest.

explanation.text: Rests are grouped by beat, just like notes. When more than one beat is silent, write a separate rest for each beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 3/4: a crotchet, then two crotchet rests.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: crotchet, crotchet rest, crotchet rest.

explanation.caption: Two silent beats in 3/4: two crotchet rests, one for each beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 3/2: a minim, then two minim rests.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: minim, minim rest, minim rest.

explanation.caption: The same idea in 3/2, where each beat is a minim: two minim rests.

explanation.text: In triple time the rule is a convention: write a separate rest for each silent beat, rather than one longer rest that joins two beats. It keeps every beat easy to see.

If a whole bar is silent, a whole-bar rest is used. In most times it is the semibreve rest, which hangs from the fourth line of the stave (4/2 is the exception: it uses a breve rest). Whole-bar rests are not part of the questions here.
One beat, one rest. The exception for whole bars is the semibreve rest.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 3/8: a quaver, then two quaver rests.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: quaver, quaver rest, quaver rest.

steps: Beat 2 and beat 3 are silent, so each gets its own quaver rest.
Every beat can be seen clearly.
demonstration.textAlternative: A bar of 3/8 with a quaver and two quaver rests.

hints: Each beat shows its own rest, except that a two-beat rest may fill half of a four-beat bar.

feedback.correct: Yes: each silent beat has its own rest.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Mark where each beat starts, then regroup.
